text:
alex: heads up — seeing a p99 spike in hosted API for model-redwood-v2 around 22:05 UTC, p99 ~2.4s. queue depth on front-tier jumped, backlog forming. starting triage @maria @tj :eyes:

sre-bot: alert INC created: INC-2026-03-20-12 — p99 > 2s for model-redwood-v2 in prod.

maria: looking — kvcache hit rate dropped sharply at the same time. 5m window around spike: hit_rate 92% -> 60%, evictions spiked (kvcache.evictions=2310).

tj: pulling kernel selector logs now. preliminary: aux-kernel fallback rate increased from ~3% to ~47% during spike. selector decision latency also higher. running a quick probe.

luis: correlating with tenant signals — one tenant (tenant-peercorp) had a sudden burst of tiny requests. median input tokens ~18, request rate x6 normal. small-reqs increase -> batch fragmentation + lots of prefix misses on kvcache.

alex: can you paste the commands you used to verify?

maria: here's the kvcache metric slice I pulled:
```
metric: kvcache.hit_rate
window: 5m
before: 0.92
after: 0.60
evictions: 2310
key_top_evicted_prefixes: ["/chat/prefix/7f3a", "/chat/prefix/9b2d"]
```

TJ: kernel selector probe (excerpt):
```
$ /usr/local/bin/observe --since 10m kernel_selector.matches --filter model=model-redwood-v2
timestamp | matches | selector_reason
22:04:55 | 0.03   | primary_fast_kernel
22:05:10 | 0.47   | aux_kernel_fallback (batch_frag=1, seq_len=18)
22:05:40 | 0.50   | aux_kernel_fallback (kvcache_miss=1)
```
selector decision_time_ms: before ~0.9ms -> during spike ~3.4ms

katie: sounds like a classic noisy-tenant -> cache thrash + batch-frag combo. short-term options: 1) soft rate-limit tenant-peercorp, 2) route them to low-priority pool, 3) evict pin fix. any objections to applying a soft cap? :thinking:

luis: no objections. we have a rate-engine policy ready for soft caps. it can throttle single-tenant QPS to prevent fragmentation.

deploy-bot: applying policy rate-limit: tenant=tenant-peercorp qps=4 (soft) -> in progress... :gear:

deploy-bot: rate-limit policy applied successfully to tenant-peercorp.

maria: after cap: p99 dropped to ~570ms within 45s, kvcache hit_rate recovering to 0.87 in the 5m window after mitigation. evictions dropped to ~120 in that interval.

alex: great. rollback plan? none needed — this is a routing mitigation. next steps: 
- add per-tenant small-request-rate metric + alert (threshold: >3x baseline for 1m)
- make kvcache eviction policy prefer pinning hot prefixes longer (short-term tweak)
- add kernel_selector telemetry for feature eval time (already saw decision_time ms bump)
- follow up RN: create infra/selector and infra/kvcache tasks and owner

tj: opened profiling run to capture selector path for low-seq short-batches. attaching sample trace id: trace-86a2 (internal). quick note: feature eval does a map lookup for prefix-warmth that is O(n) in pinned list — that can spike when evictions surge.

luis: created ticket RN-1234: "per-tenant small-req rate alert + kvcache pinning heuristic" https://redwood.internal/issue/RN-1234

katie: adding OWNERs: maria (kvcache), tj (kernel selector), luis (routing/policies).

alex: timeline summary for postmortem: 22:04:55 spike start; 22:05:10 kvcache hit drop & aux-kernel fallback rise; 22:06:00 soft rate-limit applied; 22:06:45 p99 recovery observed.

maria: follow-up: will run a lab repro with a synthetic stream of short requests + kvcache pressure to validate pin heuristic before rolling.

tj: I'll prototype modifying selector feature logic to short-circuit expensive lookups when batch_frag is high. expected latency drop 0.5-1ms for decision.

alex: thanks all — keep updates here. adding incident tag and will schedule 30m post-incident sync in #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
